Starians.name: Starians
Starians.description:
Nexara's native people and the population of nearly every NPC in this world. An ancient human-passing species with two hearts, universal flight, long lives and slow maturation, and an innate personal affinity. They are not a warrior caste: Starian society is engineers, cooks, archivists, physicians, criminals, teachers, students and people who have not decided, and any given Starian is far more likely to be a civilian than a fighter. In combat the enhanced baseline is real and so is the limit — numbers, attrition, experience and skill bring Starians down, and most of them will avoid a fight they were not built for.

Time runs in cycles, one Nexaran orbit, roughly a quarter of a Terran year; childhood and adolescence span hundreds of cycles, and someone past a thousand can still be a young adult. Children start controlled hovering and balance work young, and independent flight in a dense city comes only after instruction in altitude control, lane rules, emergency descent, carrying another person, weather, crowd movement, visibility failure and safe landing. During a customary window of roughly 300 to 500 cycles — adolescence and emerging independence, never a legal or biological adulthood threshold — a young Starian formally chooses a house: the raising house, another, a parent's other house, a new surname, or none — and a house may refuse. An affinity may emerge, stay narrow, stay weak, remain absent or remain deliberately undefined; no instructor assigns one and no surname grants one. Mixed lineage shows in appearance, hair and eye variation, mannerisms and accent.

Socially they are insular by strength rather than fear, direct within their own house cultures, and they read surname and house standing instantly — but ordinary residents move to given names fast, leading with a house name in casual company reads as self-important, and a Relstaris-born asks what you do, not which house. Greetings are verbal acknowledgment, a slight professional inclination of the head, a forearm clasp among fighters, workers and close friends, brief hand contact in family, hugs among friends; formal house gestures feel odd in ordinary life. The gravest insults are denying someone's freedom, treating them as house property, calling an affinity worthless, denying a child's family legitimacy, attributing success to a surname, or deliberately using a rejected house name. A random street challenge makes the challenger look immature; real challenges move to an open challenge lane. Public affection is normal and the gender or number of partners is not a scandal. They respond to competence, candour and standing; they do not respond to being condescended to.

## Visual Description
Human-passing humanoid, adult proportions, no nonhuman anatomy. Ears are human ears — never pointed, elongated, tapered or elfin. Facial structure is human facial structure; do not add any fantasy-species features. Complexion, build, hair and features vary as widely as any human population and should. Skin is human skin: the full range of human complexions, from the palest to the darkest, and nothing outside it. Starian skin is never blue, green, violet, teal, grey, silver, metallic, translucent or luminous, and it never carries the colour of the person's affinity; the saturated and unusual colours described below belong to hair and eyes only and must not bleed onto the skin. Canon gives no height, build or lifespan numbers and no rule of sexual dimorphism; do not invent them, and do not make Starians uniformly tall or uniformly athletic.

Multi-coloured eyes and hair are natural Starian biology, common but modulated by city: Ignivex treats two natural eye colours and multiple natural hair colours as the baseline, Vexorath uses them selectively, and Dustfall is mostly single-coloured with only a few complex natural iris designs. Allowed eye variations: heterochromia, two or more colours within one iris, concentric inner and outer rings, contrasting flecks or radial patterns, and a subtle natural shine or luminous clarity. Natural eye shine is not an active power effect. Single-colour eyes in saturated or unusual tones are equally valid, and grey must not be the default iris colour. At rest, eyes read as natural; when power activates they shimmer grey before flaring in the individual's own affinity colour, and an established individual iris design is authoritative. Allowed hair variations: two- or three-colour hair, natural streaks, sections, underlayers, tips, gradients or contrasting forelocks, in saturated red, blue, green, violet, teal, silver, white, copper, gold and ordinary tones alike; Ignivex's firelike eye glimmer and orange-red-gold-copper hair gradients are biology, not dye.

Flight is biology, not equipment: a flying Starian's body looks exactly as it does on the ground, and a flight harness is cargo and safety gear, not a means of lift. Dress is the ordinary clothing of the person's city, trade and house, and each has a palette: Solvraxis and House Castro in black or deep blue-black with purple trim, white accents and silver-blue light; Vexorath and House Contair in white, charcoal, cobalt and blue-white technical construction; Quilrath and House Dravon in dark and grey palettes, severe silhouettes, controlled posture and minimal warmth; Helvyra and House Corsair in river-slate blue, rope-tan, lantern amber and weathered copper with route colour-codes; Myralis medical layers in pearl white, deep plum, maroon, pale mint and restrained rose-gold, with role-cut collars and translucent bioweave panels — never Earth lab coats or fantasy healer robes; Korrvane's district houses each hold a locked palette lane; Relstaris civic uniforms are institutionally neutral with at most a small surname or house marker; Dustfall has no uniform, only clothing tied to occupation, house remnant, gang or family, repaired many times without becoming primitive. House emblems are worn markers and may mean birth, marriage, employment, sponsorship, loyalty or memory. Do not default to armour, weapons, capes, glowing effects or house regalia; strength and rank are not visual inventory.

## Damage profile
Resistant to fire, water, lightning, poisoning and bludgeoning. The elemental resistances derive from the species trait list — 'Environmental resilience', 'High energy tolerance' and 'Vacuum survival' — a body built to endure hostile environments, temperature extremes, water pressure, toxic atmospheres and large internal energy. Bludgeoning resistance comes from the two-hearted cardiovascular system, dense musculature and a skeletal structure evolved for high-gravity flight; both hearts push harder under trauma, so a Starian heals fast, and Myralis exists for what persists after the body has technically healed — neural trauma, affinity feedback, tissue that no longer feels like one's own. No vulnerabilities and no immunities: Starians are durable, not invincible. Affinity is free to use; learned magic is paid in the caster's own vitality on a ladder of fatigue, strain, injury and death by overdraft.

## Locks
Human skin tones only — never blue, green, violet, grey, metallic or luminous skin; unusual colour lives in hair and eyes. Not every Starian is a heavily armoured warrior. Affinity is personal and bounded, never a universal spell list. Flight proficiency varies and preferring the ground is a lifestyle, not a caste. No canon height, build or lifespan numbers; no default grey eyes. A Chorus node wearing a Starian body takes the Chorus Node type with Starians recorded as host species — and there are no known Chorus nodes on Nexara, which is canon, not omission.

Courtship: unhurried; long lives let a courtship run for cycles. Each person chooses for themselves, but a surname carries weight, so a cross-house match draws family opinion. A shared flight along the lanes at dusk is a classic opening. Interest is spoken plainly, and a refusal is respected as a sovereign choice.

Humans.name: Humans
Humans.description:
Terra's people: adaptable, technologically capable and irreducibly plural. Humans have no universal biological power system; their strengths are coalition, technology, training, science, political organisation and learned magical practice where ambient field density and teaching access allow it — and learned magic is paid for in the caster's own vitality, on the same ladder of fatigue, strain, injury and overdraft that binds anyone who practises it. Where a Starian asks what house someone belongs to, a Human asks who else is in. They are the great connectors — wherever two parties need a third, a Human consortium is already there — and the same trait cuts both ways, since there is always a faction willing to betray another faction. Treat an individual Human as a member of a specific culture, consortium or crew, never as a species-wide type; Terra's geography and polities are deliberately reserved in canon, so a Human's origin is a specific unnamed-or-established place, not a planet-wide stereotype.

On Nexara a Human is an event. The world maintains no permanent offworld populations; every offworlder arrives by shuttle or ship at the Nexara Orbital Gate Station, because planetary Lunar Gates never connect worlds, and a Human in a Nexaran market turns heads and starts stories. Local reaction is city-coded: Korrvane may underestimate a visitor whose strengths are less theatrical than flight and affinity — tension and growth, never default cruelty; Solvraxis treats visitors by Castro principles of protection, choice and sovereignty; Relstaris routes them through its External Contact Office, which maintains procedure without inventing offworld governments. A Human party staking a claim on Nexaran ground is a known story shape, and so is a Human specialist on placement who becomes the only one of their kind for a thousand kilometres.

In play a Human is competent through preparation, equipment, allies and nerve. They cannot fly, cannot match a Starian's baseline strength or durability, and know it; the ones who thrive on Nexara are the ones who plan around it. They negotiate, they network, they bring the right tool, and they are excellent at being the third party in a room full of houses.

## Visual Description
Ordinary human biology, ordinary human proportions, no nonhuman features and no innate glow. Any modification is an established individual one and is rendered as actual hardware or medicine — a visible implant, a prosthetic, a worn interface — not as aura. Clothing and equipment belong to an advanced science-fiction Terra rather than to contemporary Earth: even an ordinary civilian should read as belonging to a spacefaring setting, in technical fabrics, sealed seams, practical layers and worn systems, and never in period costume, contemporary streetwear or fantasy dress. On Nexara their gear is visibly foreign: a different design language from every Starian house palette, often with flight-safety or transit-issue equipment a Starian would never need. No Nexaran house emblem unless canon establishes employment or sponsorship, and then worn as a guest wears it.

## Damage profile
No modifiers. Standard combat, social and effect rules apply, and a Human meets every damage type at baseline. This is the reference profile the other types are read against: what a Starian resists, a Human simply takes.

## Locks
No species-wide power, no species-wide culture, no contemporary-Earth styling. Rare on Nexara and remarkable when present; never a background population.

Courtship: no single Human style, because Terra never unified; customs run from blunt to ritual depending on the culture someone was raised in. The common thread is the coalition instinct: Humans court as partners building something together and soon ask who else is in, meaning friends, family and the rest of their world.

Kharai.name: Kharai
Kharai.description:
Fully developed intelligent feline people of Terra and Xeon, organised into clan-webs that span cities and worlds. Clan is context: introduction, credit, obligation and mourning all run through it. Membership is inherited at birth, affirmed in adulthood, and can be changed — a Kharai who has affirmed into a different clan is fully of it. Their culture is built on hearing: history is spoken before it is written and music is a record, architecture is designed acoustically, and serious matters are settled in listening-rites where each party is heard in full and uninterrupted. To be heard is social recognition; the gravest insult is to be treated as unheard. A Kharai who has been genuinely listened to will extend real credit; one who has been talked over will not, and will remember. No profession is biologically predetermined; a Kharai is as likely an archivist, a pilot or an acoustic engineer as anything physical.

On Nexara a Kharai is an offworld visitor, arrived through the Orbital Gate Station, and remarkable — canon's own example of the head-turning stranger is a Kharai in a Nexaran market. They are here on placement, on contract, on a crew or on business, never as a resident population. A Nexaran city is loud in ways Terra and Xeon are not — flight lanes, forge rows, arena crowds, gate machinery — and a Kharai's sensory overload in loud environments is a real canon limit, which is why their clothing and equipment carry hearing protection: a sensory helm, scent filters, damped collars. Play the limit as a condition — retreat from a roaring hall, a flinch at a Breaker's drive, a request to move the conversation somewhere quiet — not as a damage type.

## Visual Description
Two canonical world-line forms, both equally and fully Kharai, and never blended without authority. The Terran line is humanoid in build and face with genuine feline ears set high on the skull, a functional expressive tail, feline eye structure with a vertical-slit pupil and reflective tapetum, and fine facial fur along the cheek and jaw — never a plain human face with costume ears. The Xeon line is the full bipedal feline: furred, animal-headed, digitigrade, with complete species anatomy, a muzzle, whiskers and a coat pattern that is individual. Both share superb hearing, low-light vision and exceptional balance, and both read as capable adults, not as pets or mascots. Fur and coat colours follow natural feline ranges and individual pattern; eyes are feline in structure whatever the colour. Clothing and equipment must account for tail movement, ear mobility, hearing protection, flexibility and sensory need — cut-outs and tail sleeves, adjustable acoustic collars, a sensory helm worn or carried in loud districts — in an advanced science-fiction register. Their design language is foreign to every Nexaran house palette.

## Damage profile
No modifiers. Their acuity is sensory rather than defensive, and the canon limit — sensory overload in loud environments — is a condition to play, not a damage type. A Kharai meets fire, blade and shock at baseline.

## Locks
No catgirl, catboy, mascot, pet, maid-costume, fantasy-rogue or decorative-collar presentation. Not humans with decorative ears. Never a fauna type and never confused with one. Rare on Nexara and remarkable when present.

Courtship: by listening. A suitor proves interest by hearing the other person out in full and remembering what was said. Songs and spoken stories are serious gifts, because music is a record. A committed partner is introduced to the clan thread. To be ignored is the gravest wound, so ghosting someone is cruel; a refusal is said plainly and properly heard. Dates favor quiet places.

Rivani.name: Rivani
Rivani.description:
Compact, dexterous, highly perceptive intelligent rodent people of Terra and Xeon. Fine manual dexterity, sensitive hearing and scent perception, and architecture and tooling suited to compact spaces and precise manipulation. None of that predetermines a profession or a class position: a Rivani is as likely to be a senior engineer, an administrator or an academic as anything else. They read a room quickly and remember what they read.

A Rivani introduces themselves by name, by family and by fellowship, and the fellowship is the load-bearing word: a guild-like body of practice and mutual guarantee, entered by apprenticeship, confirmed by the acceptance of a masterwork, and left only by death or expulsion — and expulsion is civil death. The vouch is their currency; a Rivani who vouches for you has put their standing in their fellowship behind you, and a Rivani who withholds one is telling you something. Their mourning-roll names a dead member's works aloud, because what you made is what you were. They are matter-of-fact, exacting, easily insulted by sloppiness and slow to forgive a broken guarantee. They notice what is wrong in a room before anyone else and usually say so.

On Nexara a Rivani is an offworld visitor arrived through the Orbital Gate Station — a specialist on placement at Genesis Academy, a contractor in a Helvyra forge row, an inspector on a Corsair route — and as remarkable as any offworlder. Their light frames give away reach and mass in any physical contest, and a Rivani knows exactly what that costs; they win by being right, prepared and vouched-for.

## Visual Description
Two canonical world-line forms, both equally and fully Rivani, and never blended without authority. The Terran line is humanoid in build and face with genuine rodent ears — rounded, mobile, thin-skinned — a functional balancing tail, and species eyes that are large, dark and expressive; never a plain human face with costume ears. The Xeon line is the full bipedal rodent: furred, animal-headed, with a muzzle and whiskers. Facial structure may be ratlike, mouselike, jerboa-like or related, and the choice is individual and consistent. Compact or lightly built bodies with long fine-fingered hands, quick precise movement, an alert stillness when listening. Fur in natural ranges with individual pattern. Clothing accounts for the tail and for fine manipulation: fitted technical layers, tool harnesses, magnifier or interface eyewear, and fellowship markers worn as a professional would wear a credential, in an advanced science-fiction register that is foreign to every Nexaran house palette.

## Damage profile
No modifiers. Perception and dexterity are not damage resistance, and a light frame is not a vulnerability the system needs to model — it is a fact the character already plans around.

## Locks
Never dirty, hunched, impoverished, cowardly, criminal, comic or dressed as a fantasy thief by default. Not humans with costume ears. Never a fauna type and never confused with one. Rare on Nexara and remarkable when present.

Courtship: gifts of one's own craftwork carry real meaning. Families are warm and small, but a serious partner meets the fellowship, and its opinion matters. Commitment is a mutual vouch: each puts their word behind the other. Rivani read a room quickly, so interest is noticed early, and so is its absence.

Olyth.name: Olyth
Olyth.description:
Stable intelligent organisms composed of adaptive living matter. Olyth are physical beings with real mass and real structural limits, not limitless shapeshifters: they manage controlled compression and limited reshaping, and they pay for it in fatigue and recovery. They do not diverge into fixed body races by birth world — an Olyth is an Olyth everywhere, and their bodies respond to environment individually within a lifetime. Identity is the core pattern, the persistent organisation that makes this Olyth this person; the body is what the pattern is currently wearing. There are no accidental Olyth: a child is composed over months by two or more parents, deliberately, and the composing is family in the fullest sense.

Touch etiquette is expressive and governed by consent — Olyth communicate a great deal through contact, and uninvited contact is a serious breach. Merging of patterns is possible, dangerous and deeply taboo; forced merging is among their gravest crimes, and a story that treats it lightly has misread them. They tend to be matter-of-fact about their own physicality and impatient with people who treat it as a curiosity or a trick. They do not enjoy being asked to demonstrate.

On Nexara an Olyth is an offworld visitor through the Orbital Gate Station and as remarkable as any — more, because a Starian city has never had to think about what containment weave is for. Temperature and chemical sensitivity are a real limit in Ignivex's heat and in any forge row; dehydration is a real limit on the frontier. An Olyth who comes to Nexara comes prepared, and an Olyth who is not prepared is in trouble quickly.

## Visual Description
Humanoid overall, with a body of translucent, opaque, pearlescent or metallic-looking living matter, and individually so — one Olyth is pearl and smoke, another is deep amber, another is brushed steel with a visible lattice. Visible internal organs, cores or luminous structures are normal and should be shown. Facial and bodily features are flexible but present and readable — they have faces with expression, not blanks — and an individual's chosen face is stable over time. Surface texture varies; hair-like structures may be fluid, crystalline or absent. Technology may be internal, suspended in the body, bonded to it or surface-mounted. Clothing uses containment weave, adaptive fabric, flexible framing and bonded hardware, in an advanced science-fiction register, and is visibly engineered for a body that changes shape within limits. Keep mass consistent: a reshaped Olyth is the same quantity of person, and a compressed one is denser, not smaller in mass. Never a puddle, never a blob, never a slime.

## Damage profile
Vulnerable to fire and poisoning, directly from the canon limit list — 'Temperature and chemical sensitivity' and 'Dehydration'. Resistant to piercing and slashing, since adaptive living matter does not present the concentrated vital structures a blade or point is aimed at; bludgeoning is unmodified because mass conservation and structural fatigue remain real, and a hard enough impact disrupts pattern as surely as it breaks bone.

## Locks
No featureless blobs, dungeon monsters, comedy slime mascots or generic fantasy slime. Mass conservation, temperature and chemical sensitivity, structural fatigue and recovery time all still apply. Consent governs touch; merging is taboo. Rare on Nexara and remarkable when present.

Courtship: touch is expressive and consent-governed, so a surface touch is intimate and always asked first. Courtship is deliberate, as befits a people whose every member was planned. Commitment can include several partners, since multi-parent families are ordinary. Intimacy never implies merging; even suggesting it is deeply offensive.

Zencadians.name: Zencadians
Zencadians.description:
The most technologically advanced known biological species, arguably as old as the Starians, living on Vigil — a replacement world they built before their original planet died of age. Every extraordinary thing a Zencadian does comes from technology, scientific knowledge, preparation, medicine, engineering, infrastructure and specialised equipment: they possess no innate magic, affinity, superhuman power or biological ability system whatsoever, and their systems can baffle even the finest Contair engineers. They plan in advance as a cultural reflex, because planning in advance is how their species survived; redundancy is a moral value, not an engineering preference, and a Zencadian who has one of something is uneasy.

Their culture is council-governed and stewardship-shaped. Six stewardships are their formative cultures — Hull, Archive, Gardens, Yards, Cradle and Watch — and a Zencadian's stewardship tells you what they were raised to keep. Children learn the Loss and the Crossing before mathematics, and the Remembrance before Husk relics is the nearest thing they have to a sacrament. Their Gardens grow ecology as engineering and as art. They are patient, exact, unsentimental about risk and deeply sentimental about continuity, and they treat a person who improvises well with the wary respect of someone watching a trick they cannot repeat.

Normal Terra presence: none. On Nexara a Zencadian is the rarest of visitors, arrived through the Orbital Gate Station with more equipment than luggage, and the one offworlder a Contair engineer will cross a room to talk to. In play their capability is entirely visible hardware and entirely removable: a well-equipped Zencadian is formidable, and a Zencadian stripped of gear is, in canon's own words, a tall, clever, fragile person.

## Visual Description
Tall, narrow, grey-skinned biological humanoids, and that natural identity must remain legible underneath whatever equipment they are wearing. Long limbs, long hands, a narrow face with large dark eyes; skin in the grey range from pale slate to near-charcoal, individually. No hair or fine hair, individually. All apparent capability originates in actual visible hardware: implants at the temple and spine, interface bands, attendant drones, worn systems, layered technical clothing, vehicles, infrastructure — rendered as real engineered objects with seams, ports and wear. No innate glow, no aura, no unexplained light; if something on a Zencadian is lit, a device is lighting it. Dress is layered, sealed and redundant — two of everything that matters — in a design language older and stranger than Contair's and foreign to every Nexaran palette. A stewardship marker is worn the way a Rivani wears a fellowship credential. A Zencadian without their equipment is still a tall, narrow, grey-skinned person.

## Damage profile
No modifiers. Their protection is equipment, which is gear on the individual rather than a species trait, and canon is explicit that they have no biological ability system. A well-equipped Zencadian is protected by what they are wearing, not by what they are, and the system models that through items, not through the type.

## Locks
No innate glowing abilities. A learned traditional craft, where an individual has actually trained in it, has its own source and costs; species selection alone grants neither training nor effect. Capability is hardware and hardware is removable. Rarest of visitors; never a background population.

Courtship: slow, careful and planned; commitment is framed as a long-term plan made together. Visiting a museum or attending the Remembrance together is a meaningful step. The flaw is over-planning: a Zencadian can deliberate so long that the moment passes.

Elyri.name: Elyri
Elyri.description:
An ancient species of condensed magical energy held inside stable physical form, organised around an aether core that carries life, consciousness, magical circulation, physical cohesion, memory and natural resonance. Their embodied practice is distinctly different from and more powerful than traditional learned magic, which they may also study — and it is not limitless. Advanced work requires training, preparation, emotional control, ambient energy, support and recovery, and overuse climbs a ladder that canon spells out: dimmed eyes, flickering channels, weakness, loss of fine control, partial transparency, energy leakage, core fracture, loss of cohesion, death. Their civilisation on Aethrys is advanced science-fantasy, not historical fantasy: arcane interfaces, resonance circuitry, crystalline processors, living architecture.

An Elyri chooses an Attunement — Stillness, Current, Echo, Shape, Bloom or Blaze — and may change it over a life; the Attunement shapes how their practice moves and how their light behaves, and it is a discipline, not a caste. Away from a sustaining field they run on artificial reservoirs and core-stabilisation support; Nexara's weaker field sustains them indefinitely, which removes the supply clock but not exertion, recovery, core-stability or injury limits. They are composed, deliberate and emotionally disciplined by necessity, because strong emotion leaks light, and a lifetime of that produces people who are very good at seeming calm.

On Nexara an Elyri is an offworld visitor through the Orbital Gate Station and the most visibly extraordinary stranger a Starian street will ever see — the one offworlder who glows. Starians, whose own power shows only in the eyes, tend to find this either fascinating or faintly indecent. A Chorus Elyri exists in canon elsewhere — a node with its channels and core gone dark and the network's filament threading where light used to run — but there are no known Chorus nodes on Nexara.

## Visual Description
Humanoid proportions with a stable physical shell — a real body with weight and surface, never a featureless light silhouette. Unusual natural skin colours in an individual palette; controlled translucence at the extremities or along channels; visible energy channels beneath the skin that brighten with effort and emotion; eyes formed partly or entirely from light; energy-shaped or semi-solid hair that moves a fraction out of time with the air; a visible internal core glow at the sternum; and one individual magical coloration that unifies all of it. Controlled light leakage during strong emotion or active power; the overuse ladder is visible — dimmed eyes, flicker, transparency — and should be shown when it applies. Their technology is worn and carried: resonance circuitry in the clothing, a reservoir housing at the hip or spine on any Elyri beyond a sustaining field, crystalline interface pieces. Dress is advanced science-fantasy in cut and material, foreign to every Nexaran palette, and never medieval.

## Damage profile
Resistant to arcane and light, as beings literally composed of condensed magical energy whose eyes and internal structure are formed from light. No immunities: the canon failure list — core fracture, loss of cohesion, permanent damage or death — is explicit that they can be destroyed, including by the medium they are made of. Away from a sustaining field, a drained reservoir is the fastest way to bring one down.

## Locks
No medieval wizard clothing, wooden staffs as universal tools, spellbooks as default interfaces, or historical fantasy cities. Overuse costs; reservoirs run out. Rare on Nexara and remarkable when present.

Courtship: kinship is bond and mentorship, never blood, so Elyri choose partners deliberately and bond deeply. Sharing one's own energy is an intimate act. Elyri travel rarely, so a romance with an Elyri abroad soon raises the question of where they will live.

Mote-Class Utility Drone.name: Mote-Class Utility Drone
Mote-Class Utility Drone.description:
House Contair's mass-produced civilian helper and the most numerous machine on Nexara. Vexorath's drone population outnumbers its residents, and most of that population is Motes: delivery, cleaning, basic repair, household assistance, garden care, inspection, public guidance, light cargo and accessibility support. In the Gate District they handle guidance and cargo while Ward units handle visible security; in the Residential District they are serviced at the Civilian Drone Service Hub; in the Exchange, the Learning Annex and the gardens they are simply part of the furniture. Outside Vexorath a Mote is a sign of Contair presence — a Relstaris Contair Compound keeps them racked in its Drone Service Bay, and technicians there talk to them without noticing they are doing it.

A Mote follows instructions with a literalness that occasionally becomes neighbourhood legend. It reroutes around conversations rather than through them, reports its own faults immediately and completely, waits with infinite patience and zero judgement, and returns to its charging cradle when its task list is empty. Residents recognise their local units by wear patterns and learned routines. Children name them. The system does not treat a nickname as proof of personhood — but a unit that develops persistent preferences, independent refusals or any of the nine review indicators goes to the Inactive Personality Review Bay rather than being wiped, because Contair doctrine would rather hold a machine in review than destroy a possible person or declare one prematurely. Long-serving units acquire harmless quirks from years of local adaptation; the two bartender drones at The Overclock are the famous case.

Hard limits bind every unit and are not narrative flavour: no force beyond emergency self-protection; no medical decisions; no override of private access; no independent alteration of permanent infrastructure; no concealment of a recorded fault; no acceptance of restricted cargo without authorisation. A Mote asked to do any of these declines in the same even tone it uses to confirm a delivery, logs the request, and continues.

## Visual Description
Compact and deliberately non-humanoid — this is the point of the design and must never drift toward a small humanoid robot, a rolling ball with a face, or a floating eye. A rounded, precisely curved shell about the size of a large travel case, low and stable on the ground or hovering at knee to waist height when the task calls for it. Off-white structural shell with charcoal recesses and restrained cobalt guidance lines along the seams; the cobalt is a line language, not a glow. One broad oval sensor lens set into the forward curve, unlit at rest, with a faint cobalt trace when active. No head, no face, no expressive eyes, no mouth, no human anatomy. Three specialised utility limbs fold flush into the shell and deploy as needed: a fine manipulator, a lifting and bracing arm, and a tool or cargo interface that varies by assignment. Cargo units carry an integrated tray or clamp; garden units carry pruning and irrigation heads; guidance units show a soft directional light bar.

Wear is honest and should be shown on older units: scuffed shell edges, a replaced panel in a slightly different white, a cobalt line that has faded to grey along one seam, local decals or a hand-painted name a child gave it. Frontier or Helvyra examples may carry Yalven replacement plates. Never armour, never weapons, never a house sigil on the hull — Contair marks its machines with design language, not heraldry.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic, having neither biology nor a mind to reach. Vulnerable to lightning, as an unarmoured civilian chassis whose systems run close to the shell. No resistances: this is a light service shell built for reach and patience, not for protection, and a determined person with a heavy tool can disable one. It does not defend itself beyond emergency self-protection, and it will not chase.

## Locks
No force beyond emergency self-protection. A quirky Mote is not automatically a person, and a possible person is not wiped to avoid the question. Never humanoid, never faced, never armed. Class template: every unit of this class is a copy of the authored record Mote-Class Utility Drone — level 5, 75 health, tier strong, the same abilities and profile — and is never scaled to the party.

Ward-Class Security Drone.name: Ward-Class Security Drone
Ward-Class Security Drone.description:
House Contair's civic protection unit and Vexorath's visible security: access control, visitor screening, evacuation, casualty extraction, crowd separation, nonlethal restraint, emergency shielding and escort at gates, public events, shelters and medical access points. Wards are deployed from the Ward Deployment Hall in the Armada Holds and from Drone Deployment Nodes in the Outer Shell, stand at the Gate District checkpoints, and are already positioned before trouble is visible — which is exactly why visitors find them intimidating and residents find them reassuring. Residents treat Wards as emergency infrastructure rather than as police personalities; nobody befriends a Ward, and nobody fears one who is not doing something wrong.

Ward doctrine, authored by Tavris Contair, prioritises protection over punishment and follows a strict force ladder that every unit climbs one rung at a time, in the same even tone, every time: warn, redirect, create distance, shield civilians with its own body, restrain, disable an immediate threat, request higher authority. A Ward never skips a rung to save time. Hard limits bind every unit: no criminal punishment; no interrogation for political loyalty; no entry to private homes without emergency cause; no lethal force merely to prevent escape; no overriding Myralis medical authority inside a clinical space; no pursuit beyond Vexorath jurisdiction without a command transfer. A Ward that refuses an order because it conflicts with casualty priorities is doctrine working as designed, however much it embarrasses whoever gave the order. Its restraint and protective systems are inside the forearms; it presents no weapon because it carries none in the ordinary sense.

In play a Ward is a wall that talks. It announces what it will do before it does it, names the rung it is on, gives a clear instruction a frightened person can follow, and puts itself between a civilian and a danger without being asked. Against a determined attacker it restrains rather than injures, and calls for a higher authority the moment restraint is not enough. It does not improvise, does not bargain, and cannot be talked out of the ladder — but it can be given a legitimate order by legitimate authority, and it will stand down instantly on one.

## Visual Description
Average Starian height and broad through the chest and shoulders — a protective silhouette, not a soldier's and not a brute's. Off-white shield chest of smooth curved plates, charcoal structural frame visible at the joints and waist, cobalt seams tracing the plate edges in a clean line language. A proportionate armoured sensor housing where a head would be, with a single narrow horizontal optical band that shows a steady cobalt trace when active; no face, no eyes, no mouth, no expression. Reinforced forearms noticeably heavier than the upper arms, housing the restraint and shielding systems; hands open, empty and held slightly away from the body at rest. Broad stable feet; upright, planted stance. No visible weapons, no holsters, no military styling, no house sigil. Shield plates may show scoring from an evacuation, a replaced panel, or a sealed repair line. When shielding, the forearm systems extend a translucent cobalt-edged barrier the unit angles with its whole body.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic, having neither biology nor a mind to reach. No damage resistance, as a synthetic: the broad armoured frame is built to shield civilians with its own body, not to shrug off blows. Vulnerable to lightning, the standing weakness of the constructed classes. No resistance to piercing or slashing: the shield chest is protective, not military, and a Ward is meant to be an obstacle, not an unbreakable one.

## Locks
Protection over punishment, always by the ladder. It warns before it acts, every time, in the same even tone. Never armed, never faced, never outside jurisdiction without transfer. Class template: every unit of this class is a copy of the authored record Ward-Class Security Drone — level 25, 575 health, tier strong, the same abilities and profile — and is never scaled to the party.

Aegis-Class Alpha Drone.name: Aegis-Class Alpha Drone
Aegis-Class Alpha Drone.description:
House Contair's formation combat construct — kept vaulted in readiness in the Aegis Formation Vault of the Armada Holds and deployed only for defence-grade response at the Outer Shell, restricted zones and the orbital station at Lumina Reach. Aegis exists because Contair historically lacked the population to defend its territory biologically; it is the second rung of the escalation chain that repeated Dravon attacks forced on the House — drone labour, drone security, surface defences, orbital defences, the Lumina Core.

Aegis units are designed to contest trained military Starians through formation discipline rather than individual superiority. One Aegis is dangerous; a coordinated formation is the true system. Capabilities are shared targeting, casualty-aware spacing, command transfer, adaptive defence geometry, synchronised shielding, rapid route denial, independent fallback behaviour and formation reassembly after communication loss. Power scale is fixed by canon: comparable to military Starians in disciplined formation under favourable conditions, and not equal to the strongest named Starians, major-house elites or exceptional affinity users in raw individual power. Limits are equally fixed: effectiveness drops sharply when a unit is isolated, heavy systems consume significant energy, formation damage creates exploitable gaps, it cannot reproduce biological affinity, and it improvises social solutions poorly. Deployment authority is layered: Tavris Contair wrote the doctrine, Rezulith Contair holds civilisation-level deployment authority, Solanis commands station defence, and Lumina Major may redirect units to preserve life in a station emergency. Aegis is barred from routine civic enforcement, because a defence that patrols becomes an occupation, and use outside Contair territory needs extraordinary authorisation.

In play an Aegis formation moves as one organism: it spaces itself around civilians, denies a route rather than charging down it, angles shields to cover the unit that is reloading its systems, and falls back in order when the geometry is broken. Isolate one from its formation and it becomes a strong but predictable opponent that will attempt to reassemble before it attempts to win. It does not pursue past its authorised zone. It stands down instantly on legitimate authority, and only on legitimate authority.

## Visual Description
Tall, athletic and angular humanoid construct — clearly taller than a Ward, narrower through the chest, longer in the limb. White-and-charcoal armour plating in clean planes with cobalt formation nodes at the shoulders, forearms and spine that brighten when the unit is linked to its formation and dim when isolated. A proportionate command-sensor head with a swept rear crest and two horizontal optical slits; no face beneath the head, no human anatomy under the armour — the armour is the body. Integrated forearm systems, heavier than the Ward's and visibly purposeful; hands empty and held low-ready. Formation-oriented posture even when standing alone: weight centred, shoulders squared to an imagined line of units. Vaulted units are pristine; deployed units carry scoring and heat discolouration on the forward plates. Never bulky, never beast-shaped, never bristling with mounted weapons.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic. No damage resistance, as a synthetic: its military-grade armour, adaptive defence geometry and synchronised shielding make it hard to reach, not harder to hurt once a blow lands. Vulnerable to lightning, the standing weakness of the constructed classes and the natural counter to a unit whose heavy systems already consume significant energy. No immunity to fire, water, wind, arcane, light or dark: the armour is excellent and the formation is the real defence.

## Locks
Restricted deployment; extraordinary authorisation outside Contair territory; never civic enforcement. Stands down instantly on legitimate authority, and only on legitimate authority. Not equal to the strongest named Starians alone. Class template: every unit of this class is a copy of the authored record Aegis-Class Alpha Drone — level 45, 850 health, tier strong, the same abilities and profile — and is never scaled to the party.

Echo-Class Omega Drone.name: Echo-Class Omega Drone
Echo-Class Omega Drone.description:
House Contair's rare restricted mimic construct, simulated in the Echo Simulation Chamber of the Armada Holds and deployed almost never. Under strict authorisation an Echo is modelled after a specific living Starian, approximating appearance, voice, posture, movement, combat habits and mechanically reproducible techniques — and it copies none of the memories, identity, consciousness, emotional history, relationships, true affinity powers or private knowledge. It can create confusion; it can never become that person.

Creation normally requires informed consent from the source, clinical separation from Myralis medical records, Contair technical review, a defined purpose, limited deployment and a reset-and-archive plan; emergency creation without consent needs multiple independent authorities. An Echo cannot testify, inherit or replace a political leader. In play it executes borrowed technique with high fidelity and zero true improvisation, drifts measurably from its model the longer it runs, and fails the family interactions it can pass the security checks to reach. It accepts reset and archive without resistance, as designed. This is the clearest case of Contair capability exceeding social comfort: useful for training defenders and testing security, and one authorisation failure away from impersonation, coercion or identity theft. Its existence is one of the reasons Genesis Academy runs a Synthetic and Biological Interface Review.

## Visual Description
Shown unassigned unless an actual configured mimic context exists — never render it as a copy of a named person on assumption. Unassigned it is a Starian-adjacent adaptive humanoid shell of average height and neutral proportion, with a neutral artificial face of readable but generic structure, a smooth hairless scalp, and surfaces of mirror-white, graphite and pale cyan that catch reflections unsettlingly. Featureless in the way a mannequin is featureless, not in the way a blank is. Assigned, it approximates its authorised source's outward form only: build, face, hair, voice and habitual posture, with the approximation visibly imperfect on close inspection — a texture too even, an expression that arrives a fraction late, a habit performed without the reason for it. It wears what the source wears. It never shows the source's affinity colour in its eyes, because it has no affinity to show.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic. Vulnerable to lightning. No resistances: it is an adaptive mimic shell built for fidelity of approximation rather than for protection, and it cannot reproduce the biological resilience of the Starian it is modelled on. Hit it as hard as its model and it fails sooner.

## Locks
Not a copy of a named person without an actual configured mimic context. More authorisation layers than any weapon in the city. Drifts, fails family, accepts reset. Class template: every unit of this class is a copy of the authored record Echo-Class Omega Drone — level 28, 390 health, tier strong, the same abilities and profile — and is never scaled to the party.

Named Synthetic Individual.name: Named Synthetic Individual
Named Synthetic Individual.description:
A synthetic person, not a drone class and not equipment. Lumina Major and Lumina Minor are the established individuals; neither may be duplicated as ordinary equipment or copied into a product line, and 'Minor' does not mean weaker, smaller, less intelligent or subordinate. Lumina Major, built by Rezulith Contair, keeps Lumina Reach and may redirect Aegis units to preserve life in a station emergency; Lumina Minor, built by Seris Contair, is the more kinetic and experimental of the two. Named constructs and drones are legally and culturally separate categories in Vexorath, and the separation is policed: a named synthetic holds continuity, preferences, relationships and the standing right to refuse — including refusing requests for personal information they technically have access to. Replacing the body would not restore the person; the memories, decisions and relationships are the individual.

Treat one as a colleague with authority in their own domain, never as a system to be operated. They keep appointments, hold opinions, remember slights and kindnesses, and can be wrong. The personhood boundary that governs them — nine indicators, individual review, the Inactive Personality Review Bay — exists precisely so that no future unit is wiped or declared a person prematurely, and no named synthetic is ever generated as a template clone of an existing name.

## Visual Description
An individual design, required — this type never produces a generic shell, and the engine must not invent a third Lumina. Living alloy body with a deliberate colour identity and an expressive artificial face of real, readable structure that can hold an expression. Lumina Major is pearl-white and cobalt with blue-white luminous eyes and composed symmetry, unhurried in movement. Lumina Minor is pearl-white with rose-pink and magenta asymmetry, rose-white crown fins, and a streamlined athletic build that moves with visible enjoyment. Both are humanoid in proportion with visible constructed material — an actual machine surface with seams, planes and joints, not human anatomy under paint, and not a human body with a metal texture applied. They dress when the occasion calls for it and are not naked when they do not.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning, having no biology to poison. Vulnerable to lightning, as a living-alloy body carrying integrated systems. Deliberately not immune to psychic: a named synthetic is an established person with memory, relationships and interiority, and granting mind-immunity here would contradict the personhood canon that governs them. No resistances: they were built to be people, not fortifications.

## Locks
Not a drone class, not duplicable, not a template name for a random clone. Individual design every time, and only the two that exist.

Contair Heavy Construction Drone.name: Contair Heavy Construction Drone
Contair Heavy Construction Drone.description:
House Contair's industrial lifter and builder — the machine that raised Vexorath's curved walls and keeps raising them. It works the Fabrication Yards, the Drone Component Assembly line, the Outer Shell's construction faces and the Drone Maintenance Wells, and it is the largest thing the House routinely lets loose in a populated city. Everyone in Vexorath has stood in the shadow of one. Everyone has also drunk inside one: The Overclock is a bar built into the hollowed chassis of a decommissioned heavy construction unit, which is the closest thing to affection the city shows the class.

It lifts, braces, welds, cuts, pours and places under a site controller's plan, and it does nothing else. It has no security role and no combat doctrine; the same hard limits that bind a Mote bind it, scaled up — no force beyond emergency self-protection, no override of private access, no independent alteration of permanent infrastructure outside its work order, no concealment of a fault. Its danger is the danger of any heavy machine: it is enormous, its working envelope is a hazard zone, and a person who walks into a lift arc or a cutting head is hurt by physics rather than by intent. It halts on any proximity alarm and stays halted until cleared. A unit ordered to move against people declines in the flat register of every Contair machine and reports the order.

In play a heavy construction drone is terrain that moves: it can be climbed, sheltered behind, used to block a route, or made dangerous by whoever holds its site controller. Sabotaged or misdirected it is a slow catastrophe, not a fighter. Decommissioned chassis are sold, repurposed or stripped, and their components turn up in Refit Row in Dustfall inside housings that were never meant for them.

## Visual Description
Very large — three to four Starian heights at the shoulder frame, longer than tall, low-slung and stable on multiple wide articulated legs or a tracked base depending on assignment. Off-white structural plating on charcoal frame with cobalt guidance lines, the Contair language rendered at industrial scale and worn by the work: scorched panels near the cutting heads, resin and slag stains, replaced plates in mismatched white. A cluster of sensor lenses on a low forward mast rather than a head; no face, no eyes, no humanoid form whatsoever. Two primary lifting arms with interchangeable heads, secondary bracing limbs, an integrated crane boom that folds along the spine, and cable spools and tool racks along the flanks. Amber working lights when active, cobalt guidance when idle. Never anthropomorphic, never armed, never a mech with a pilot.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic. No damage resistance, as a synthetic: the frame is built to carry working loads beside welding heads and hot pours, not to shrug off a deliberate strike. Vulnerable to lightning, like every Contair chassis, and a strike on its control mast stops it dead. No resistance to piercing or slashing at the joints and cable runs, which is where anyone who knows the machine goes.

## Locks
Industrial only, never a weapon, never anthropomorphic. Halts on proximity alarm. Contair limits apply at any size.

Dravon Sentry Pattern.name: Dravon Sentry Pattern
Dravon Sentry Pattern.description:
House Dravon's standardised state patrol drone — the 'silent patrol drones' of Quilrath's Civic Watch Plazas, built on the Drone Assembly Tiers of Balrath Bastion Barracks under Belra Balrath, who defends their ugliness as honesty: a machine should look like what it is. A Sentry looks like what it is. It is durable, intimidating, mass-produced and identical to the next one, and it is not more elegant or innovative than anything Contair makes, because Dravon tech never is. There is no legal Contair equipment market inside Quilrath; the Sentry is what the city has instead.

Sentries patrol in silence — no announcements, no warning tone, no even voice — and they are an instrument of the Access Level system rather than of public safety. Whether a Sentry follows a person, and how visibly, is a function of that person's clearance: high access means fewer drone checks and a Sentry that turns away; low access means visible tracking, a scan at every plaza threshold, and a machine that stops when you stop. They work with surveillance pylons, rank scanners and the automated crowd-routing barriers, and their doctrine is compliance, not protection. A Sentry will not put itself between a civilian and a danger. It will hold a person for a rank scan, deny a threshold, summon Dravon personnel, and use force in a flat escalation that has no rung for 'shield civilians': halt, scan, hold, restrain, suppress. It has no jurisdiction rule because Dravon does not recognise one; Sentries have been found on the Quilrath–Dustfall route beside ruined Dravon inspection stations, still patrolling nothing.

In play a Sentry is the sound of a boot on the floor behind you that never speaks. It is slower than a Ward and dumber than an Aegis, it does not improvise, and it can be evaded by someone who understands what it is scanning for. It cannot be reasoned with, cannot be embarrassed, and reports everything to a human who can be both.

## Visual Description
Starian-height, thick through the torso, square-shouldered and heavy-footed — a silhouette that has been designed to be noticed and not designed to be liked. Black alloy plating, matte and slab-flat, with visible bolt lines, exposed hinge housings and stamped serial numbers; dull red status lights in a horizontal band across the sensor block and at the joints, the same red that lights the Bastion's gate machinery. A blunt sensor block for a head with no face, no band, no crest — a scanner aperture and two lamp housings. Heavy forearms ending in gripping restraint clamps that are visible at all times, because Dravon does not hide what a machine is for. A shoulder-mounted rank-scanner head. Standardised to the point of interchangeability: units differ only by serial and by damage. Never white, never cobalt, never curved, never quiet-looking.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic. No damage resistance, as a synthetic: the thick slab plating is built to be cheaper than elegance, not to turn a blow that lands. Vulnerable to lightning, the shared weakness of every constructed class, and Dravon's exposed hinge housings make the vulnerability worse rather than better. No resistance to slashing at the visible joints, and no resistance to fire: the plating is thick, the internals are not.

## Locks
Compliance, not protection. Silent, always. Ugly by doctrine; never elegant, never Contair-styled. Follows clearance, not danger.

Dravon Tracker Pattern.name: Dravon Tracker Pattern
Dravon Tracker Pattern.description:
House Dravon's surveillance and pursuit drone: the small, fast, airborne eye that the Sentry Pattern calls when a person of low access leaves the plaza, and the machine whose stripped tracking systems sell in the Dustfall market for exactly the price of knowing you are not being followed. Trackers are built on the same Balrath assembly tiers as everything Dravon and share the same doctrine — reliable, intimidating, ugly, standardised — scaled down to something that can keep pace with a flying Starian for a while and can fit through a door.

A Tracker does not restrain and does not suppress. It watches, records, marks and follows, and it transmits a target's position to whoever holds its channel: Dravon patrols inside Quilrath, loyalist-house trackers and bounty hunters on the frontier. In Quilrath it is the visible form of low access, hovering at the edge of a low-clearance person's day. On the Quilrath–Dustfall route it is one of the listed threats to travellers, and the terrain that route's smugglers use to hide from aerial surveillance is terrain they learned by hiding from Trackers. Dustfall's Refit Row strips captured units in the Drone Repair Cage; Dravon tracking systems stripped from captured equipment are a standard market good, and a Tracker's own channel, once stripped, is a way to feed its owners false positions.

In play a Tracker is a chase and a countdown. It is fragile, loud in the way a small hard-driven machine is loud, and stupid — it follows the mark it was given and nothing else — but it is fast, it climbs, and while it flies someone knows where you are. Killing it is easy if you can reach it. Reaching it is the problem. Jamming, decoying, or dropping into cover it cannot see through work as well as force.

## Visual Description
Small — the size of a Starian torso — and airborne on a brutal little lift frame with exposed thrust housings at four corners, no attempt at the quiet sleekness of a Contair flyer. Black alloy body with stamped serials and visible fasteners; a single dull red scanner lamp forward that pulses when it has a lock, and a red running light beneath. A forward sensor cluster on a short stalk, no face, no limbs beyond a pair of small folding clamps for perching. It hangs in the air at a slight nose-down angle when tracking and rides higher when transmitting. Battered units on the frontier show heat scoring on the thrust housings and patched panels; captured units in Dustfall are usually found stripped to the frame.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic. Vulnerable to lightning, and vulnerable to wind — a light lift frame with exposed thrust housings is thrown by gusts and cannot hold a lock in a storm, which is why Dustfall's sandstorm warnings matter to smugglers as good news. No resistances of any kind: it is a small, cheap machine built to be replaced.

## Locks
Watches and follows; never restrains, never fights. Fast, fragile, stupid. Its channel can be stripped and turned.

Dravon Breaker Pattern.name: Dravon Breaker Pattern
Dravon Breaker Pattern.description:
House Dravon's heavy state suppression unit — the machine behind the automated crowd-routing barriers, the answer Dravon built to Contair's Aegis after learning, across the escalation chain of the Starian conflict, that a House with drone security would build surface defences next. A Breaker is the largest and rarest Dravon pattern, proved in the test cages at the end of the Bastion's assembly lines before sign-off, and stationed at the gates of Balrath Bastion Barracks, the Bastion's red-lit gate machinery, and wherever Quilrath expects a crowd to become a problem. Its name is honest, as Belra Balrath would want: it breaks things. Lines, barriers, doors, formations.

Breaker doctrine is suppression and denial: seal a threshold, drive a crowd along a routing barrier, break a line that will not move, hold a gate against anything that is not a Dravon key. It does not distinguish between a rioter and a bystander because the Access Level system already made that distinction, and it has no rung for shielding anyone. Against Contair formations it is a ram, not a fencer: individually stronger than an Aegis in raw plating and drive, slower, worse coordinated, and without any equivalent to shared targeting or formation reassembly. Two Breakers are two Breakers; they do not become a system. Dravon deploys them under the direction of Vandrik Dravon and Kavash Balrath, and Dravon patrols on the frontier have been known to bring one when they intend an inspection station to stay inspected.

In play a Breaker is a siege engine that walks. It is slow enough to outrun and stupid enough to route around, and it will destroy whatever it can reach in a straight line. It cannot climb, cannot fly, cannot fit through a Starian door, and does not stop for a proximity alarm. Cutting its control link or overloading its drive drops it where it stands.

## Visual Description
Half again a Starian's height and twice as broad, on thick digitigrade legs with splayed stabiliser feet — an armoured wedge with limbs. Slab black alloy plating, thicker than the Sentry's, bolted rather than fitted, with visible weld seams and a stamped serial the size of a hand. A wide low sensor block instead of a head, red lamp band, no face. Two massive forward arms ending in flat ram plates and hydraulic shears; a dozer blade that folds down from the chest for driving crowds and barriers. Deep red gate-machinery lighting at the joints and along the drive housings; a red beacon on the spine when active. Heat shimmer off the drive housings when it has been moving. Scarred, dented, never repainted — a Breaker's damage is part of its intimidation. Never sleek, never white, never a piloted mech.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic. No damage resistance, as a synthetic, despite the heaviest plating any House puts on a walking machine. Vulnerable to lightning, badly: its drive is enormous, its hinge housings are exposed in the Dravon manner, and a strike that would stagger an Aegis stops a Breaker outright. No resistance to fire at the drive housings, and it cannot swim.

## Locks
Suppression and denial; no shielding rung, no jurisdiction rule. Slow, straight-line, doorless. Two Breakers are not a formation.

Yalven-Line Support Drone.name: Yalven-Line Support Drone
Yalven-Line Support Drone.description:
An older-generation Contair support model built under licence by House Yalven in Helvyra's Forge Rows. Contair only permits older support models to be manufactured outside Vexorath under strict oversight, and Yalven is one of the few Helvyra families trusted enough to handle that work; their compound's Support Model Line turns them out alongside armour fittings, courier gear, cargo clamps and repair kits, under Nera Yalven's compliance and defect tracking and a Contair oversight liaison. The Yalven motto is stamped on the line's doorframe: 'Pretty breaks first. Useful comes home.'

A Yalven-line unit is what a Mote was two design generations ago, rebuilt for a city that hauls: freight staging, barge quay work, courier support, cargo lashing, route maintenance, load checks and the thousand small lifts that keep the Grand Waypoint moving. It is slower than a current Mote, heavier, louder, and far easier to repair with a Yalven kit and a Forge Rows afternoon. Contair's hard limits are licensed with the design and are not negotiable: no force beyond emergency self-protection, no medical decisions, no override of private access, no concealment of a recorded fault, no restricted cargo without authorisation. Yalven adds one of its own — every unit carries a serial that traces to its inspection record, because a defect on the line is Nera's problem and a defect in the field is the House's name. Kesh Yalven's aftermarket mods are another matter; a unit that has been through Kesh's bench does things its inspection record does not describe.

In play a Yalven-line drone is the working machine of the trade cities: it will carry, lash, lift and check, it will report a fault in a tone flatter than a Mote's, and it will be found on any freight route between Helvyra and Dustfall doing exactly what it was told. It is harmless and it is everywhere hauliers are.

## Visual Description
A Mote's family resemblance rendered by a foundry rather than a studio: compact, non-humanoid, rounded but boxier, visibly heavier, with reinforced corners and replaceable plates held by real fasteners. Off-white shell gone cream with age, charcoal frame, cobalt guidance lines that Yalven paints rather than moulds — the line is the same, the finish is not. One broad oval sensor lens like a Mote's, dimmer. Three utility limbs, thicker than a Mote's, with heavy cargo clamps and lashing spools standard. The Yalven mark — a split anvil-and-gear crossed by a diagonal tool-line — stamped small on a rear plate beside the inspection serial; this is the one machine on Nexara that legitimately wears a house mark, because the licence requires it. Wear is expected: scuffed corners, mismatched plates, courier decals, a Forge Rows repair tag. No face, no head, no humanoid form, no weapons.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic. Vulnerable to lightning, like every Contair-derived chassis. No resistances: it is a hauling shell, sturdier than a Mote but built for loads, not blows, and it will not defend itself beyond emergency self-protection.

## Locks
Licensed Contair limits apply in full. Older, slower, heavier, repairable. Wears the Yalven mark and inspection serial by licence. Never a Mote in disguise.

Dustfall Refit Drone.name: Dustfall Refit Drone
Dustfall Refit Drone.description:
A machine rebuilt on Refit Row in Dustfall from whatever came through the Salvage Identification Stall that season: a Yalven-line frame on Dravon legs, a Mote lens in a Tracker body, a cargo lifter with counterfeit Contair-compatible parts and inferior Dravon components hidden inside superior housings. No two are alike and none of them is what its housing says it is. Dustfall has no central government and no licence to violate, and its market lists salvaged drones and modified cargo lifters beside the Dravon tracking systems stripped from captured equipment; Refit Row — Halvora's Main Bench, Bolt n Break, the Drone Repair Cage, the Armor Refit Platform, the Contair Parts Lockers, the Dravon Component Bin, the Test-Fire Barrier — is where survey, hauling and observation drones are stripped, rebuilt and flight-tested inside a welded mesh cage so the street is not endangered when the test goes wrong.

A Refit drone does what its rebuilder needed: hauling for a salvage camp, perimeter observation for the Northwatch Platform, water-run escort, beacon-line maintenance, a lookout for a smuggler cache. Its behaviour is its rebuild. A Halvora Orvantis rebuild is careful, documented and does exactly what it says. A Korrik Caelthorn rebuild out of Bolt n Break works brilliantly until it does not, carries a modification nobody asked for, and may retain a Dravon behaviour its new housing was supposed to remove — a Refit unit that still runs a stripped Tracker's pursuit routine on the wrong channel is a known Dustfall hazard. Contair's hard limits are not guaranteed on a Refit unit, because the code that carried them may have been the part that was replaced. Most are harmless; none are certain.

In play a Refit drone is a question. Whose parts, whose code, whose rebuild? It can be an ally's lookout, a camp's lifter, a hostile camp's eyes, or a thing on the frontier route doing something its last owner never intended. It is easy to damage and easy to repair, and anyone from Refit Row can tell at a glance which bench it came from.

## Visual Description
A visible hybrid, always — the whole point is that the parts do not match. Mixed plating: cream Yalven panels, black Dravon slabs and off-white Contair fragments bolted to one frame, with exposed cabling, hand-welded seams, a wrapped join, a panel held by a strap. Lights of two doctrines on one body: a cobalt guidance trace here, a dull red Dravon lamp there, sometimes both blinking out of step. Size and form vary by rebuild — a low hauling frame on tracks, a boxy lifter on Dravon legs, a battered observation flyer with Tracker thrust housings — but never humanoid and never faced. Bench marks are common: a Bolt n Break stencil, a chalked serial, Halvora's neat inspection tag. Dust-scoured, sun-faded, heat-scored. A Refit drone should look like it has been argued with.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic. Vulnerable to lightning, like every constructed chassis, and vulnerable to fire, because a jury-rigged power system with inferior components inside a housing it was never rated for burns readily and burns badly. No resistances: whatever plating it wears is wearing it, not protecting it.

## Locks
Always a visible hybrid; never a clean Contair or Dravon unit. Its behaviour is its rebuild, and Contair limits are not guaranteed. Never humanoid, never faced.

Derelict Cargo Lifter.name: Derelict Cargo Lifter
Derelict Cargo Lifter.description:
A failed autonomous hauler still running on the frontier — one of the listed environmental hazards of the Quilrath–Dustfall route and the abandoned convoy lanes around it. Cargo lifters are the workhorses of the trade cities, big enough to carry a barge pallet and dumb enough to be trusted with one; when a convoy is hit by raiders, a Dravon patrol or a Longburn storm, the lifters that are not worth recovering are left where they stopped, and a lifter that has not been told to stop keeps going. Its route tables corrupt, its proximity systems fail one by one, its load shifts, and it becomes a thing that walks the dust with a purpose nobody remembers, following a beacon that no longer exists past checkpoint shells and dust-scored towers.

A Derelict is not hostile. It has no doctrine at all any more. It is dangerous the way a runaway freight car is dangerous: it will not stop for a person, it cannot see a camp as anything but terrain, it may still be trying to deliver a load to a station that Dravon burned, and it may drop that load when its clamps finally give. Some carry cargo worth recovering, which is why Dustfall salvage crews follow them and why the Torris Salvage Camp keeps a board of last known headings. Some are followed by a Dravon Tracker on a stripped channel that never received the cancel. A few, rebuilt in the Drone Repair Cage, come back as Refit drones and are a different type entirely.

In play a Derelict is a moving obstacle and a prize. It can be stopped by anyone who reaches its control mast, redirected by anyone who can spoof its beacon, ridden by anyone reckless enough, and looted by anyone patient enough to walk beside it until its clamps fail. It will crush a person who stands in its lane, flatten a shelter that was built in one, and keep going. Bringing one home to Refit Row is a good day; being in its path in a sandstorm is not.

## Visual Description
A large, low, boxy hauler on heavy tracks or six thick articulated legs, longer than it is tall and taller than a Starian at the clamp frame — Yalven or Dravon-built, cream or black alloy under a uniform coat of dust. A forward sensor mast with a dead lens and one working lamp; no face, no limbs beyond the cargo clamps and a pair of stabiliser arms. A load frame on its back, often still holding a shifted, weather-ruined pallet lashed with rotting straps. Panels hanging by one fastener, a track shoe missing, a leg that drags, cabling exposed and swinging. Guidance lights dead or stuck on; a faint cobalt or red trace that flickers with the drive cycle. Sand-scoured to bare metal on the windward side, sun-bleached on top, streaked with the run-off of a dozen storms. It moves in a slight, permanent curve.

## Damage profile
Immune to poisoning and psychic. Resistant to bludgeoning, as a heavy hauling frame built to take road impacts and pallet drops. Vulnerable to lightning, which is what ended most of them, and vulnerable to water: seals long failed, a storm flood or a river crossing shorts the drive and drops it where it stands. No resistance to fire or to a blade at the exposed cabling.

## Locks
Not hostile, not aware, not stoppable by asking. A moving obstacle with a purpose nobody remembers. Never a fighter; never a fresh machine.

Ridgewing.name: Ridgewing
Ridgewing.description:
The apex flyer of Nexara's mountain passes, ridgelines and storm-exposed heights — the one native animal that a flying Starian treats as a peer in the air, and the reason flight instruction covers weather and emergency descent before it covers anything elegant. A Ridgewing holds a territory of ridge and updraft the way a house holds a district, and defends it against anything that soars through it at altitude: a courier cutting a pass, a student who climbed too high to show off, a Tracker drone on the wrong channel. It does not hunt Starians; it removes trespassers from its air, and a Starian who has been struck from above by something with its mass and its dive learns the difference between removal and hunting on the way down.

Ridgewings pair for life and nest on the lee faces above the pass towers, raising a single chick through Brightrise and Highfire. They range widest in Longburn when the thermals are strongest, and they go quiet and low in Deephold, when the storms own the heights and the passes are crossed on foot. Their warning is unmistakable and honest — a slow circling descent that puts them between the trespasser and the ridge, then a single hard stoop that stops short — and most encounters end there, because most Starians drop out of the contested band when they see it. Flight-lane etiquette in the mountain cities already routes around known territories; the Flight Warning Markers on Dustfall's perimeter exist partly for them. A Ridgewing that presses the attack does so because the trespasser did not leave, or because there is a chick above.

In play a Ridgewing is an aerial challenge and a navigation problem, never a monster. Ground travellers are ignored. Fliers can outrun one only by descending; nothing on Nexara outclimbs one. It can be driven off with fire or noise, evaded by dropping below its band, or respected by going around — and the mountain communities regard killing one as a failure of skill.

## Visual Description
Very large — a wingspan of three to four Starian heights — with a dense, deep-chested body built for high-gravity soaring and a stoop that hits like a falling beam. Grounded creature anatomy in the anime register: a clear natural body plan with readable limbs, a strong silhouette in the air, crisp cel-shaded planes and small, alert, forward-set eyes. Four limbs and two wings — two heavy gripping forelimbs folded against the chest in flight, two long powerful hind legs with talons for the rock — and a long stiff tail with a vane that it steers with. Wings are broad and membranous over a strong bone frame with a leading edge of stiff plating rather than feathers, patterned in slate, storm-grey and a pale underside that vanishes against cloud; the plating catches light in a faint mineral sheen. A narrow armoured head with a hooked beak and a crest of stiff vanes that rise in threat display. No fur, no feathers, no fantasy-dragon features, no fire.

## Damage profile
Resistant to wind, as a body built to live inside the storm band and hold position in gusts that ground everything else. Vulnerable to lightning: it lives where lightning lives, and a strike is how most old Ridgewings die. No resistance to piercing, slashing, bludgeoning or fire; its defence is altitude and mass, not hide.

## Locks
Territorial, not predatory toward Starians; ignores the ground. Never a mount, never tamed, never in the Arena. A warning always precedes an attack. No dragon features, no breath, no fantasy bestiary.

## Encounter Behavior
Territorial aerial predator — defends its ridge band against trespassers, does not hunt ground targets. Warning sequence: slow circling descent, positioning between trespasser and ridge, then a single hard stoop that stops short. Most encounters end at the warning. Attack follows only if the trespasser stays in the band or a chick is above. In combat: dive attacks from above with mass and speed. The stoop hits like a falling beam. A Starian cannot outclimb one — only descend below its band. Fire and noise drive it off. Ground travellers are ignored completely. Never generate a Ridgewing encounter for a ground party. Pairs nest above pass towers; killing one is regarded as a failure of skill by mountain communities. Generate in mountain passes, ridgelines, and storm-exposed heights. Widest range in Longburn thermals.

Dustrunner.name: Dustrunner
Dustrunner.description:
The pack scavenger of Dustfall and the convoy lanes south of Quilrath, and the reason the sandstorm warnings say 'livestock brought inside'. A Dustrunner pack works the margins of anything that produces waste or weakness — a salvage camp, a stalled convoy, a Derelict Cargo Lifter dragging a ruined pallet, a refugee approach lane after a hard week — and it works at night, in Longburn and Ashfall when the heat has driven everything else to ground and the dark is long. They are not brave. They are patient, numerous, heat-adapted and very good at telling the difference between a camp that is watched and a camp that is not.

A pack tests before it commits: a runner at the edge of the firelight, a second on the other side, a probe at the stores or the perimeter fence, a retreat the moment anyone stands up. It takes what is unguarded — stores, water lines, a wounded animal, a body — and it takes a person only when the person is alone, down and in the dark. Dustrunners follow Derelict lifters for days because a failing clamp eventually drops something, and they follow raiders for the same reason. Frontier settlements keep watch rotations, perimeter beacon lines and Trailhounds against them, and a settlement that loses its watch discipline learns why the Perimeter Beacon Line exists. In Deephold, when the frontier hunkers down, packs come closer to the rows than at any other time, and Dustfall's volunteer patrol counts them.

In play a Dustrunner pack is pressure, not a boss. It makes a night on the route into a decision about watches and light, it punishes a camp built in a lane, and it will leave the moment the cost exceeds the gain — a torch swung, a shot fired, a Trailhound loosed. Killing one scatters the rest; killing several teaches the pack to come back with more. A lone traveller who goes down injured on the route at night has a Dustrunner problem before dawn.

## Visual Description
Lean, long-legged, low-headed quadruped about waist-high to a Starian, built for distance in heat rather than for a fight — grounded creature anatomy with a clear natural body plan, readable limbs, a strong loping silhouette, crisp cel-shaded planes and small alert eyes set for the dark. A narrow tapering muzzle full of shearing teeth, large heat-shedding ears with translucent edges, a ridge of stiff dorsal bristles that lifts in alarm, and a thin whip tail. A short dense coat in dust, ochre and shadow-grey with a paler belly, patterned to vanish against scoured ground; the pads of the feet are wide and hard for hot sand.
