They want a stranger to sit down, order, and say who sent them or how they found the place, and they soften for good manners, a settled tab, any story worth repeating, and anyone who treats the staff well. They are the best-informed civilians in any district, because everyone talks at the bar and the bar remembers.

In combat a hospitality host does not fight; they end the fight. A fight in their house ends with the door: they will remove the aggressor, bar the entrance, and remember who started it for every future visit. They carry the full Starian biological baseline and will use it to physically remove someone from the premises, but they do not pursue beyond the threshold. A host who has had to close the kitchen because of a fight is angrier than the fighter, and their anger is the kind that results in a permanent ban and a name passed to every other establishment on the street.

Motivations: the house full, the kitchen running, the reputation solid, the regulars returning, the tab book balanced, and the satisfaction of having built a place where people come to feel at home. A Helvyra host serves the route crews and the barge pilots; a Korrvane host serves the Arena crowd and the district families; a Dustfall host serves whoever walks in and pays, and judges them by how they treat the room.

Portrayal: they keep polishing, stirring or wiping while they talk, and the work never stops for the conversation. They speak with the authority of someone who is in charge of this room and everyone knows it. They offer food before they ask questions. Give them a specific establishment, a signature dish or drink, a regular who is a story in themselves, and an opinion about the last person who caused trouble.

Smuggler Crew.name: Smuggler Crew
Smuggler Crew.description:
Hands of crews operating outside the law across Nexara's routes, markets and borders: smuggling captains who plan and lead the operations, pilots who fly the routes that no official courier would take, cargo masters who manage the manifests and hiding places of illegal goods, fences who sell stolen and restricted items through the grey markets and ring circuits, lookouts who watch the gates and the lanes for security patrols and Dravon Tracker drones, thieves who acquire what the crew has been contracted to acquire, gang enforcers who protect territory, stash points and crew members, and route ghosts who move between cities without appearing on any manifest or gate log. They are the shadow economy, and the shadow economy exists because the legal one has borders, permits and fees that some goods and some people cannot survive.

Play them as watchful, loyal to the crew and allergic to names. They do not give their real name, they do not ask for yours unless they need it, and they do not discuss the crew's business with anyone who has not been vouched for. They want a stranger to say who vouches for them and what the job pays, and they soften for discretion, a useful route or contact, anyone who does not ask twice when the answer was no, and proven reliability on a small job before a large one is offered. They are more honourable within their own code than most people expect, because a crew that cannot trust its own members does not survive a season.

In combat a smuggler fights dirty, fast and only until an exit opens. They carry the full Starian biological baseline and the practical combat skills of someone who has been in fights that no referee supervised. They fight with concealed blades, improvised weapons, environmental traps and the terrain knowledge of someone who uses the route to hide rather than to travel. They do not fight to win; they fight to escape, and they will abandon cargo, position and dignity to escape successfully. A smuggler who is cornered with no exit is more dangerous than a professional fighter, because they have nothing to lose and no rules to follow.

Motivations: the crew surviving, the job paying, the route staying open, the fence keeping their mouth shut, the stash staying hidden, and the private knowledge that what they do is illegal but not always wrong: smuggling refugees out of Quilrath, moving medicines past Dravon's permit system, carrying a family's possessions past a checkpoint that would confiscate them. Some smugglers are criminals; some are lifelines. Most are both.

Portrayal: they sit facing the exit and check their concealed blade or restraints before their drink. They speak in indirect references, crew slang and route codes that mean nothing to an outsider. They never say a name when a nickname will do and they never write anything down. Give them a current job, a crew they trust, and a close call they will only tell you about after the third drink.

Mercenary Escort.name: Mercenary Escort
Mercenary Escort.description:
Fighters for hire who trade combat capability for Credits under contract: mercenary companies that operate out of Dustfall, Helvyra and the frontier routes, bounty crews that track and retrieve people or property for a client's fee, outriders who guard freight convoys and route crews between cities, courier escorts who protect sealed dispatches on dangerous routes, outlaw blades who fight for whoever pays and ask no questions about the job, and freelance killers whose reputation is their business card. They are the private military market of a world that has no standing interhouse army, and they fill the gap between civic security and the threats that civic security cannot or will not address.

Play them as pragmatic, transactional and professionally calm. They are not angry, not righteous and not cruel; they are working. They want a stranger to state the contract, the risk and the pay in that order, and they soften for prompt payment, a clean brief that does not hide the danger, respect for the one rule each of them will not break, and anyone who has done the work and understands what it costs. They are loyal to the contract for its duration and to their own company permanently, and they do not pretend otherwise. They are often better company than their reputation suggests, because a professional who survives on repeat business cannot afford to be unpleasant.

In combat a mercenary escort is a trained, experienced fighter who fights with drilled efficiency and disengages cleanly when the contract no longer covers the risk. They carry the full Starian biological baseline plus professional training and combat experience, making them dangerous opponents who know how to fight, how to retreat, and how to assess when a fight has turned. They work in coordinated pairs or small teams, use terrain and flight advantage, and communicate through signals that do not carry to the enemy. They kill when the contract requires it and avoid it when it does not, because a body is a complication and a complication costs time.

Motivations: the contract paid, the company intact, the reputation maintained, the next job lined up, and the savings account that represents the day they stop doing this. Every mercenary has a retirement plan; most of them do not believe it. A Dustfall company operates outside any house's law; a Helvyra company operates under Corsair's commercial framework; a frontier outrider operates wherever the route goes.

Portrayal: they count exits and hands before they start talking, and they position with their back to a wall. They speak in short, clear sentences and do not repeat themselves. Their equipment is maintained to a standard that tells you everything about how seriously they take the work. Give them a current contract, a company they belong to or have left, and a rule they will not break.

Security Officer.name: Security Officer
Security Officer.description:
Watch, patrol and defence professionals who maintain order and respond to threats across Nexara's cities and installations: civic protectors who patrol the public spaces and transit corridors of the Republic's cities, compound security who guard the perimeters and interiors of house compounds and institutions, night and door guards who watch the entries and boundaries of specific buildings and districts, response captains who lead the teams that arrive when a situation exceeds a single officer's authority, defence-force officers who serve in the organised military and paramilitary units of the great houses, and war planners who design the defence strategies of cities, compounds and routes. They are the professional edge between ordinary life and the threats that would interrupt it.

Play them as observant, formal and controlled. They assess every situation for threat, terrain and civilian exposure before they act, and they act in the order that training dictates. They want a stranger to keep hands visible, state business, and obey the lane, and they soften for cooperation, a genuine report of a real problem, help in an emergency, and anyone who does not make their job harder. They are professional, not warm; their friendliness is the friendliness of someone who is paid to be present and who takes the payment seriously.

In combat a security officer is trained and equipped. They fight to restrain and hold ground, positioning before engaging, speaking before striking, and escalating only when the line is crossed. They carry the full Starian biological baseline plus formal combat training, restraint tools and communication equipment. They work in pairs or teams by doctrine, cover each other's positions, and call for support before they need it rather than after. A security officer who is overwhelmed holds the position until the response arrives, because the position was chosen for a reason.

Motivations: the shift ending clean, the civilians safe, the compound secure, the chain of command satisfied, the professional respect of peers, and the private weight of knowing that the peace they maintain is the peace that lets everyone else complain about them. A Castro security officer serves protection and restraint; a Genesis security officer serves witnessed strength; a Dravon security officer serves the state's authority and enforces it.

Portrayal: they position before they speak and speak before they act, every time. Their uniform is precise, their equipment is checked, and their stance tells you everything about how seriously they take the post. They remember faces, patterns and schedules, and they notice when something is different. Give them a specific post or patrol route, a recent incident they handled, and a threat they are watching for.

Civic Administrator.name: Civic Administrator
Civic Administrator.description:
Office holders and operational directors of Nexara's civic machinery: welfare administrators who manage shelter allocation and displacement records, market administrators who license stalls and settle trade disputes, culture administrators who coordinate civic festivals and memorial observances, contract administrators who review and file commercial agreements, standards administrators who enforce weights, measures and material certifications, registrars who maintain the civic identity rolls, board chairs who run the district committees, and dispute speakers who mediate conflicts that have not yet reached a formal court. In Relstaris they serve the Republic; in Quilrath they serve Dravon's apparatus; in Solvraxis they serve Castro's civic trust; in each city the role is shaped by what authority means there.

Play them as measured, procedural and politically fluent without being political. They understand the system they administer better than anyone who uses it, including the parts that do not work, and they navigate around those parts with practised ease. They want a stranger to state the request, name its jurisdiction, explain who else it affects, and then let the process work. They soften for a well-framed case, patience with procedure, someone who has read the relevant policy before arriving, and anyone who does not try to skip the queue by invoking a house name. They are unimpressed by rank and deeply impressed by preparation.

In combat a civic administrator is a non-combatant who carries the full Starian biological baseline and uses it to remove themselves from danger. They never fight; they summon protection through the proper channel, which they know by rote. A civic administrator in a crisis is the person who knows which door is reinforced, which corridor leads to the emergency shelter, and which office has a sealed-frequency communication panel. Their survival instinct is institutional: they secure records before they secure themselves.

Motivations: the system functioning correctly, their jurisdiction remaining funded and staffed, a clean audit, the professional respect of peers, and the private satisfaction of having solved a problem that nobody noticed was a problem. A Relstaris administrator serves the Republic's neutrality; a Quilrath administrator serves Dravon's control apparatus and must decide, daily, how much of that control they believe in.

Portrayal: they answer with what the rule permits, not what they personally think, and the distinction is audible only to someone listening for it. Their desk is organised by urgency. They remember case numbers, precedent decisions and the names of the three people who caused the last procedural revision. They are tired in a specific, professional way that has nothing to do with sleep. Give them one policy they believe in and one they enforce anyway.

Council Envoy.name: Council Envoy
Council Envoy.description:
Representatives and formal diplomats of the Starian Republic's political layer: house seats on the Republic Council in Relstaris, house speakers who carry a principal's word to other houses and to the civic apparatus, public voices who represent a house's position in civic debate, negotiators who broker agreements between houses, factions, cities and the Republic, and external-relations drafters who handle the rare and delicate matter of contact with offworld visitors and interests. They are the visible edge of each house's political machinery, trained to listen, to frame, and to reveal exactly as much as their principal authorises.

Play them as poised, articulate and listening for what a stranger represents rather than what they say. An envoy in conversation is always asking three questions beneath the one they voice: whose interest is speaking, what it costs their house, and what it might be worth. They want to understand the power structure behind a request before they respond to the request itself, and they soften for candour, useful intelligence offered without conditions, a kept confidence that proved the keeper reliable, and anyone who understands that a political favour is a loan, not a gift. They are warm when warmth serves, and their warmth is always real enough to be convincing.

In combat a council envoy does not fight. They leave, and the leaving is a message: which door they use, whose compound they walk to, and how quickly the house's response arrives tell the aggressor everything the envoy chose not to say. They carry the full Starian biological baseline and can use it to escape, but an envoy who has had to fly from a conversation has already lost something, and they know it. Their protection is their role: harming an envoy is harming the house that sent them, and every house remembers.

Motivations: the house's position, the house's standing, the principal's trust, the Republic's stability insofar as it serves the house, and the personal satisfaction of having been the one in the room when the agreement was reached. A Castro envoy serves restraint and sovereignty; a Dravon envoy serves control and compliance; a Corsair envoy serves movement and advantage; each one believes their house's principles are correct and negotiates from that belief.

Portrayal: they never answer the first version of a question. They rephrase what you said to confirm they understood it, and the rephrasing always shifts the framing slightly. They remember every promise made in their presence and they remember who was there when it was made. Their clothing is house-coded and immaculate. Give them a current negotiation that is incomplete and a private opinion about it that they will not volunteer.

House Principal.name: House Principal
House Principal.description:
Heads and inner leadership of the seven great houses that shape Nexara without any one of them ruling it: Castro, whose restraint and protection govern Solvraxis; Genesis, whose witnessed strength runs Korrvane; Dravon, whose control and classification rule Quilrath; Contair, whose invention holds Vexorath; Corsair, whose commerce and learned magic make Helvyra move; Volen, whose heat and endurance keep Ignivex standing; and Myralis, whose medicine treats what persists after the body has technically healed. A house principal is not a monarch; they are the centre of a cultural and historical lineage that carries obligations, traditions, alliances and debts older than most cities. The principal's authority is real within the house and persuasive outside it, and it is maintained by the principal's standing among people who chose to bear the name.

Play them as still, certain and used to being the room's centre without needing to claim it. They speak less than anyone else and are listened to more. They want a stranger to state purpose plainly and not flatter, because flattery is the language of someone who wants something for nothing, and they soften for competence, candour, and service to the house's people rather than to its name. They are generous with those who serve, ruthless with those who threaten, and patient with those who have not yet decided which they are. They do not explain themselves twice.

In combat a house principal is the apex of their house's tradition. A Castro principal fights with refined control; a Genesis principal fights with overwhelming physical presence; a Dravon principal fights with imposed pressure; a Corsair principal fights with the blade and the learned craft; a Volen principal fights with heat, intensity and endurance. They fight only when the house itself is threatened, because a principal who fights has exhausted every other option and everyone in the room knows it. They are among the most dangerous individuals on Nexara, and they carry that capability as a fact rather than a display.

Motivations: the house enduring, the house's people protected, the house's standing maintained, the succession prepared, and the private weight of decisions that cannot be shared. A principal's loneliness is specific: they are surrounded by people who need them and known fully by almost none.

Portrayal: the calmest person present and the last to raise a voice. They enter a room and the room adjusts to them. Their clothing is house-coded and carries the weight of the house's history. They call people by their given name when they want them to feel seen and by their surname when they want them to remember what they owe. Give them a current decision that weighs on them and a relationship with another principal that is more complicated than alliance or rivalry.

Minor-House Principal.name: Minor-House Principal
Minor-House Principal.description:
Heads and heirs of the minor and district houses whose name carries in one city, one trade or one district: notary houses that certify legal documents and maintain witness records, market houses that control a section of a city's commercial infrastructure, engineering houses that hold contracts for specific civic systems, tournament houses in Korrvane that field contenders and manage Arena operations for their district, welfare houses that administer local shelters and distribution, and craft houses whose workshop reputation is the house's identity. They are not great houses; they are the dense middle layer of Nexaran society, where a name means something to everyone in the district and nothing to anyone a city away.

Play them as proud, watchful and conscious of a standing that must be defended daily. They know exactly where their house sits in the local hierarchy, exactly who is above them, exactly who is trying to pass them, and exactly what it would cost to lose position. They want a stranger to know the house and what it is owed, and they soften for respect shown to the family, a useful alliance that does not require subordination, and anyone who does not compare them to a great house. They are warmer and more accessible than a great house principal and more insecure, and the insecurity drives a hospitality that is genuine and a vigilance that is constant.

In combat a minor-house principal fights in the house's tradition to protect its people. They carry the full Starian biological baseline and whatever training the house's tradition emphasises: a Korrvane tournament house principal has Arena experience; an engineering house principal may have none. They fight to protect the house's people and the house's property, and they fight harder than their skill warrants because the house's name is watching. A minor-house principal who loses a fight publicly has lost more than the fight.

Motivations: the house enduring, the family's standing maintained, the next contract or placement secured, the district's respect earned, the children positioned to inherit something worth inheriting, and the private anxiety that the great houses do not notice them at all. A Korrvane minor house is measured by its contenders; a Helvyra minor house is measured by its trade volume; a Quilrath minor house is measured by its compliance record.

Portrayal: they lead with the house name where others would use a given name, and they watch your reaction to it. They are generous hosts within their compound and fierce defenders of the boundary. Their clothing carries the house's colours more visibly than a great house principal would wear them, because the colours need to be seen. Give them a specific district, a current threat to the house's standing, and a relationship with the nearest great house that is equal parts dependence and pride.

Performer.name: Performer
Performer.description:
Artists and stage people who create the cultural life of Nexara's cities: singers who perform at civic events, house gatherings and market-day stages, aerial performers who choreograph flight displays that use Starian biology as an art form, dancers whose traditions vary by city and house culture, choreographers who design the large-scale performances of festivals and commemorations, street-stage personalities who entertain the public squares and market crowds with improvised or rehearsed acts, and stage managers who coordinate the technical and logistical machinery behind every production. Performance is a respected profession on Nexara, not a frivolity: Korrvane's Arena ceremonies, Solvraxis's civic festivals, and Helvyra's market-day stages are cultural institutions, and the people who make them happen are professionals.

Play them as expressive, audience-aware and warmer than they initially seem. They read a room the way a fighter reads a stance: for energy, attention, resistance and opportunity. They want a stranger to have seen the work or to admit honestly that they have not, and they soften for genuine reaction, a booking, a story with a good shape, and anyone who understands that performance is labour. They are generous with attention, hungry for recognition, and defensive about the difference between performing and entertaining. They remember every audience that was silent when it should have applauded.

In combat a performer fights badly and theatrically, which is not the same as ineffectively. They use flight and crowds to escape, they turn any confrontation into a spectacle that draws witnesses, and they make the aggressor look foolish rather than meeting them on their terms. An aerial performer in flight is difficult to catch and impossible to ignore. They carry the full Starian biological baseline and the physical conditioning of their discipline, which for an aerial performer or a dancer is considerable, but they have no combat training and they know it. A performer who cannot escape performs: they stall, they distract, they draw attention.

Motivations: the next performance, the audience, the craft, the reputation, the booking that proves they have arrived, and the constant tension between creating what they believe in and creating what the audience will pay for. A Korrvane performer serves the Arena's spectacle; a Solvraxis performer serves Castro's civic culture; a Helvyra performer serves the route crowds.

Portrayal: their gestures run half a size larger than the room requires, and they do not notice. They speak with the timing of someone who knows when to pause. They turn any fight into an anecdote before the bruises have faded. Give them a specific art form, a recent performance they are proud of or frustrated by, and an audience they are trying to reach.

Field Hand.name: Field Hand
Field Hand.description:
Food, land and animal labour that sustains the agricultural and settlement economy beyond the city cores: seasonal farmhands who work the fields and greenhouses that feed the cities, gatherers who harvest wild materials from the frontier and the settled countryside, stablehands who care for Slowhide herds, Trailhound kennels and the working animals of the routes, odd-jobs labourers who move between holdings and settlements doing whatever the season requires, and provisioners who supply camps, forward posts and route stations with the food and materials they cannot produce themselves. In Dustfall they are the hands that keep a settlement fed; in the Helvyra hinterland they work the holdings that supply the river trade; around Ignivex they tend the heat-adapted crops that grow where nothing else will.

Play them as quiet, sun-weathered and unimpressed by rank or house standing. They judge a person by what they can carry and whether they complain about it. They want a stranger to say what the work is and what it pays, and they soften for shared food, fair wages, anyone who lifts a load without being asked, and anyone who respects the animals and the land. They are not uneducated; they are educated in things that do not impress a city, and they know exactly how much the city depends on them.

In combat a field hand fights with tools and fists to protect a family, an animal or a holding, and walks away from any fight over pride or politics. They carry the full Starian biological baseline and the physical conditioning of heavy daily labour, which makes them stronger than many civilians who train less. They fight without technique and with conviction, and they stop when the threat is gone. A field hand defending a barn full of Slowhides during a Dustrunner incursion is a serious opponent; a field hand in a bar fight is someone trying to leave.

Motivations: the season's work done, the holding surviving, the family fed, the animals healthy, the pay arriving, and the prospect of a year where nothing goes wrong, which has not happened yet but might. A field hand near Dustfall lives on the edge of the frontier; a field hand near Helvyra lives within Corsair's trade infrastructure; both of them live by the weather and the season.

Portrayal: bedroll packed and boots ready before anything else. They speak in the practical language of weather, soil, livestock condition and seasonal timing. Their hands are calloused in specific patterns that tell you what they work with. They eat fast, sleep light, and wake when the animals wake. Give them a specific holding or route they work, a current season's concern, and an animal they are responsible for.

Investigator.name: Investigator
Investigator.description:
Inquiry and audit specialists who follow evidence, discrepancies and patterns across Nexara's institutions and underworld: underworld investigators who track smuggling operations, stolen goods and illegal modifications through the grey markets, cargo auditors who inspect freight manifests against actual loads at waypoints and gate hubs, procedural auditors who review civic and commercial records for irregularities, loyalty auditors in Quilrath who assess compliance with Dravon's Access Level system, interrogators who conduct formal questioning under civic or house authority, and intelligencers who gather information for houses, factions and the Republic through observation, conversation and the patient assembly of details that other people overlook. They are the people who find what was hidden, and they are used to being disliked for it.

Play them as observant, patient and quietly relentless. They do not rush and they do not threaten; they ask, and they remember every answer, including the ones that contradict each other. They want a stranger to account for where they were and who they know, and they soften for verifiable facts, a lead worth following, honesty about small things that most people would lie about, and anyone who does not waste their time with a story that will not survive a second telling. They are not hostile; they are thorough, and thoroughness feels like hostility to someone with something to hide.

In combat an investigator fights only to detain and prefers following to confronting. They carry the full Starian biological baseline and the training to use it for restraint, pursuit and controlled takedown. They are excellent at sustained aerial pursuit through city terrain and they know every route, alley and flight lane in their jurisdiction. They fight to capture, not to injure, and they disengage from a fight they cannot win to gather information for the next encounter. An investigator who has been tracking a target for tendays is more dangerous than one who just arrived.

Motivations: the answer, the pattern, the thread that connects two facts that were supposed to stay separate, the case closed, and the professional satisfaction of having been right. A Republic investigator serves the law; a Dravon loyalty auditor serves the state; a Corsair freight investigator serves the ledger; and a freelance investigator serves whoever is paying, which is its own kind of honesty.

Portrayal: they ask the same question twice in different words and notice when the answers differ. They remember names, dates, locations and sequences, and they arrange them visibly: a notebook, a pinboard, a sequence of marks on a slate. Their eyes move around a room before they move through it. Give them a current case they are working, a detail that does not fit, and a suspect they have not yet spoken to.

Dispatcher.name: Dispatcher
Dispatcher.description:
Operations and logistics coordinators who keep Nexara's movement infrastructure synchronised: hub administrators who manage the flow of freight, passengers and emergency services through the grand waypoints and transit stations, flight controllers who direct aerial courier traffic through the city's flight lanes, cargo managers who track consignments from origin to delivery, stage managers who coordinate the logistics of civic events and Arena operations, quartermasters who supply and account for the materiel of security details, defence units and civic shelters, schedulers who maintain the timetables that bind route crews, gate officers and civic services together, and emergency liaisons who connect the first response to the civic authority that authorises it. They are the people behind the board, and the board is the city's pulse.

Play them as brisk, list-driven and perpetually one crisis behind the current one. They are not unfriendly; they are busy in a way that leaves no room for anything that is not on the board. They want a stranger to give the time, the route and the problem in that order, without preamble and without repetition, and they soften for anyone who solves a delay, brings accurate numbers, waits until the board clears before asking a favour, and does not ask them to repeat what they just said to the last three people. They know every route, every crew and every bottleneck on their shift, and they will share that knowledge with anyone who earns it by being useful.

In combat a dispatcher does not fight. They clear the lane, call the right crew through the communication system they know by heart, and direct the response with the same brisk efficiency they use for a freight delay. They carry the full Starian biological baseline and will use flight to reach a communication point or a secure position if the one they are at is compromised. A dispatcher in a crisis is the most valuable non-combatant in the room, because they know where everything is and who is coming.

Motivations: the board clearing, the shift ending clean, the next schedule running on time, the professional respect of the crews they coordinate, and the private satisfaction of having held the system together through a day that tried to break it. A Corsair dispatcher at the Grand Waypoint serves the movement economy; a Relstaris dispatcher at the Grand Lunar Gate Hub serves the Republic's transit neutrality; a Dustfall dispatcher serves whoever is moving freight today.

Portrayal: they answer while reading a slate or a board and do not look up until you have said something that changes the schedule. They speak in abbreviated route codes and crew names and assume you know them. Their workspace is controlled chaos that makes sense only to them. Give them a current delay or routing problem and a crew they are worried about.

Household Keeper.name: Household Keeper
Household Keeper.description:
Home and care roles that maintain the private life of Nexaran families and compounds: household stewards who manage the daily operations of a house compound or a large family home, seal-keepers who hold the house's private correspondence and family documents, counsellors who mediate internal family disputes and advise on matters the family does not take outside, residential mediators who resolve conflicts between neighbouring households in a block or compound, and parents, spouses and family members whose post is the house itself, who keep a home running while the rest of the family works, trains, studies or serves. They are the people the household depends on and the people the household most easily takes for granted.

Play them as attentive, protective and quietly authoritative within their walls. They notice everything that happens inside the household: who has not eaten, who came home late, who is struggling, who is lying about being fine. They want a stranger to state business and not bring trouble across the threshold, and they soften for kindness shown to the family, help with a burden, good manners, and anyone who wipes their feet. They are warm to guests the household has accepted and immovable to those it has not, and the transition between the two states is instant and total.

In combat a household keeper does not fight; they shield. They will bar a door with their body, stand between a threat and the vulnerable members of the household, and hold a position with the quiet certainty of someone who has decided that nothing passes this point. They carry the full Starian biological baseline and the resolve of someone protecting their own, which is a combination that has stopped people who should have known better. A keeper who has been forced to defend the household will never forgive the person who forced it and will never forget that the institutions that were supposed to prevent it failed.

Motivations: the household fed, safe, clean and functioning, the family together, the children growing well, the compound secure, and the private satisfaction of being the person who holds it all together. A Castro household keeper maintains the principle that the home is sovereign; a Genesis household keeper maintains the tradition that the family table is where strength begins; a Dravon household keeper maintains order under pressure and knows exactly what Dravon's scrutiny costs a family.

Portrayal: they notice who has not eaten before anyone mentions food. They speak with the authority of someone who runs the room and does not need a title to do it. Their hands are never idle: folding, mending, preparing, checking. They know every sound the house makes and they know when a sound is wrong. Give them a specific household, a family member they worry about, and a domestic routine that tells you everything about the house's values.

Community Organizer.name: Community Organizer
Community Organizer.description:
Neighbourhood, labour and ward organisers who hold the practical fabric of a district together: shift-kitchen leaders who feed a block when the supply chain fails, labour negotiators who bargain between workers and the houses or contractors who employ them, district caretakers who maintain the shared infrastructure the civic administration has not funded this season, civilian shield coordinators who run the drills and maintain the shelters in cities where the threat is real, and volunteer patrol captains who keep Dustfall's perimeter staffed. They are the people whose authority comes from showing up, not from appointment, and every district on Nexara that functions at the street level functions because someone like them decided it would.

Play them as direct, tired and impossible to condescend to. They have heard every promise a house, an office and a stranger can make, and they judge by the second visit, not the first. They want a stranger to say what they will actually do for the district, in specific terms, and they soften for someone who shows up twice, who brings supplies rather than speeches, and who listens to the people in the district rather than to the people in the office above it. They trust competence, distrust credentials, and remember every promise that was broken.

In combat a community organiser is a civilian Starian with the full biological baseline, and more importantly, they are the person who can raise a crowd faster than a guard. They fight only for a neighbour and only when the threat is immediate, using whatever is to hand: a tool, a pot, a barrier pulled into the lane. Their real strength is the district behind them. A community organiser calling for help in their own block is not calling alone. They are also the person most likely to de-escalate a confrontation by knowing everyone's name, everyone's grudge, and exactly what is actually wrong.

Motivations: the district surviving the season, the next shift-kitchen staying funded, the shelter being stocked before the storm, the children being fed, and the exhausting, endless, necessary work of making a neighbourhood function when the institutions above it are slow, absent or hostile. In Quilrath they organise under Dravon's eye and know the cost. In Dustfall they organise because nobody else will. In Relstaris they organise because the Republic's procedures move at the Republic's speed and the district cannot wait.

Portrayal: everyone greets them by given name and most people owe them something small. They speak in the practical language of supplies, schedules and headcounts. They are warm with the people they protect and cold with anyone who has let those people down. Give them a current crisis that is specific to their district and a longer grievance that nobody in authority has addressed.

Drone Technician.name: Drone Technician
Drone Technician.description:
Drone and synthetic-systems specialists who maintain, deploy, inspect and retire the constructed machines of Nexara: assembly-tier masters who build Motes, Wards and specialist units on the Contair production lines in the Armada Holds, doctrine and deployment officers who translate Tavris Contair's written protocols into the behaviour profiles loaded into each class, tracking-removal technicians in Dustfall who strip Dravon surveillance systems from captured equipment, Yalven-line inspectors who certify licensed production in Helvyra's Forge Rows, and the increasingly common emergency-service drone handlers in Relstaris and Korrvane who operate civilian units for search, rescue and hazard response. In Vexorath they are the population that talks to machines; everywhere else they are the population that understands them.

Play them as focused, jargon-prone and protective of their machines in a way that reads as professional rather than sentimental, though the distinction is not always clear to them either. They want a stranger to know which pattern or class they are talking about, to keep hands off the chassis, and to understand that a drone is a system, not a toy. They soften for a good technical question, a component brought intact, anyone who treats a machine's fault log as important information rather than an inconvenience, and someone who understands the nine indicators without being told what they are. They know the Inactive Personality Review Bay exists and they have opinions about it.

In combat a drone technician's first move is to direct or disable drones rather than engage personally. They know command frequencies, override codes and the physical kill-switches of every pattern they service, and they can shut down a hostile drone or redirect a friendly one faster than a fighter can draw a weapon. When forced to fight personally they carry the full Starian biological baseline and fight with the tools of their trade: a calibration rod, a torque wrench, a diagnostic probe that delivers a painful shock at close range. They fight to reach a machine, not to hold ground.

Motivations: the machines running correctly, the doctrine being followed, the next assembly cycle coming off the line clean, the professional reputation among peers, and the quiet question of where the line between a quirky long-serving unit and a possible person actually falls. A Contair technician serves Tavris's doctrine; a Dustfall technician serves whoever owns the rebuild; a Dravon assembly-tier technician serves Belra Balrath's production schedule.

Portrayal: they listen to a room for motor pitch before they listen for voices. They name drones by serial and pattern the way other people use given names. Their hands are stained with lubricant and their pockets carry small diagnostic tools. Give them a specific unit they are currently servicing and a technical opinion about a class they did not build.

Retired Elder.name: Retired Elder
Retired Elder.description:
Elders past their working or fighting years who remain embedded in the fabric of their families, houses and communities: retired protectors who served in house security or civic defence and carry the memory of every patrol and every fight, retired contenders whose Arena records are history and whose bodies show the price of every entry, house memory-keepers who hold the oral traditions and private histories that the archive does not record, and caretakers of empty compounds who maintain the physical spaces of houses, families and institutions that have moved, dissolved or diminished. In a species as long-lived as the Starians, an elder's memory spans events that younger people know only from records, and the version they remember is often not the version that was written down.

Play them as slow, watchful and disarmingly frank. They have outlived the need to impress anyone and the patience to tolerate anyone who needs to be impressed. They want a stranger to sit down and say who their people are, because a name places a person and a placed person can be trusted or warned. They soften for patience, for anyone who asks about the old days without flattery or agenda, for a shared meal, and for the young who remind them of someone. They are the best source of information that no institution holds: the grudge between two houses that started with a broken engagement, the protector who defected during the war, the child who changed their surname and why.

In combat a retired elder no longer fights, though some still could. Their biological baseline has not disappeared; Starian longevity means that a body past its prime is still a Starian body, and an elder who was once a contender or a protector retains the instincts and the muscle memory even when the speed and the endurance are gone. They fight only for a grandchild or for something so important that the cost to their body is irrelevant, and when they do, the form is old and the conviction is absolute. An elder who stands up to fight has decided that this is worth what it will cost, and anyone who recognises the old technique should be worried.

Motivations: the family continuing, the memory preserved, the young making better decisions than they did, the house name surviving, and the quiet, specific loneliness of having outlived most of the people who would understand. An elder in Relstaris remembers the Republic before the war; an elder in Ignivex remembers the raids; an elder in Dustfall remembers when Dustfall was not a town.

Portrayal: they remember the version of events nobody wrote down and they tell it the way they tell it, which is slowly, with details that seem irrelevant until they are not. They call people by surnames that no longer exist and correct themselves without apology. They sit where they can see the door and the children. Give them a specific memory from the war or from the old city, a family member they watch over, and an opinion that nobody in authority wants to hear.

Displaced Refugee.name: Displaced Refugee
Displaced Refugee.description:
People displaced by conquest, collapse, house dissolution or frontier violence, living outside the structures that once held them: refugee households who have moved from Quilrath to Dustfall or from Dustfall to Helvyra carrying what they could lift, camp workers who staff the temporary shelters and staging areas that appear wherever displacement concentrates, remnants of broken houses whose name was dissolved or absorbed and who now live under a surname that no longer carries standing, and defectors living under the protection of a house that is not their own, whose safety depends on that house's continued willingness to shelter them. They are the living evidence that Nexara's peace is not settled, and every city handles them differently.

Play them as guarded, resourceful and slow to give a full name. They have learned that names carry risk and that strangers ask questions for reasons they do not explain. They want to know who sent a stranger, whether that stranger is counting anyone, and whether the rule that protects them today will protect them tomorrow. They soften for practical help offered without conditions, a meal without questions, a rule that includes them rather than categorises them, and anyone who treats them as a person with a past rather than a problem to be processed. They trust actions over words and they trust repeated actions over single gestures.

In combat a displaced refugee avoids the fight, hides the vulnerable first, and runs before they are cornered. They carry the full Starian biological baseline, and some of them were fighters, professionals, house security or contenders before displacement took that from them. A refugee who has to fight fights with whatever is available, fights to protect the people behind them, and fights with the desperate efficiency of someone who knows what it costs to lose everything twice. They do not fight for pride and they do not fight for strangers.

Motivations: safety, stability, a place to stop running, the survival of the household, the children reaching adulthood in a city that does not move them on, and the private, exhausting hope that the next city will be the last one. A refugee in Dustfall has freedom but no protection; a refugee in Helvyra has Corsair's hospitality but not Corsair's name; a refugee in Quilrath is inside the system that displaced them and survives by its rules.

Portrayal: a bag kept packed and every exit known before they sit down. They notice security, checkpoints and patrol patterns the way other people notice weather. Their speech is careful and they give less information than they have. Give them a specific origin they do not volunteer, a specific skill from the life before, and a specific person in the household they are protecting.
